newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY WINS MUNICIPAL POLLS

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) trounced its main rival, the Congress, in the elections to the 133 wards of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. The BJP nominees bagged as many as 80 seats. The Congress was a poor second with 36 followed by independents, mainly Congress rebels, with 12 and the Janata Dal five.
The Economic Times
GREATER CAPITAL ACCOUNT CONVERTIBILITY ON THE CARDS

The Economic Survey for 1996/97 (April-March), presented by the finance minister in parliament, has called for greater transparency in laws governing foreign investment flows to attract higher foreign savings. The survey called for a review of the foreign exchange regulations for the purpose, which, in turn, implied a move towards greater convertibility on the capital account.
BOURSES CAUTIOUS AS BUDGET APROACHES

Equities held on to their previous day's prices on the Bombay bourse (BSE) as operators and institutional investors adopted a cautious stand ahead of the announcement of the budget. Save for Reliance Industries, whose price rose 2.35 percent, most other pivotals finished lower. The BSE 30-share index closed 3,356.83 compared to its previous close of 3,358.47. The National Index closed a shade lower at 1,463.07.
GLITCHES IN AVIATION POLICY TO BE IRONED OUT

A promise to resolve the remaining ambiguities in the civil aviation policy was the high-note of the Economic Survey. The survey stated that Indian Airlines would increase the dollar fare on domestic services from March 1, 1997 as a follow up to the fare hike in rupee terms from September 22, 1996. These moves would offset the estimated 600 million rupee loss in 1996/97 (April-March) on account of the revised prices of aviation turbine fuel effective July 3, 1996.
FOOD SUBSIDY TO MULTIPLY FOURFOLD

The revised estimate on total food subsidy for 1996/97 (April -March) was fixed at 61.14 billion rupees, against the budget estimate of 57.74 billion rupees for the period. The food subsidy for 1997/98 would, however, increase to 82.82 billion rupees on account of the government's decision to provide foodgrain to people below the poverty line at reduced prices.
Financial Express
CAPITAL GAINS BONDS FROM IDBI

The Industrial Development Bank (IDBI) will become the first financial institution to float capital gains bonds. It also planned to raise capital gains deposits under the Income-tax Act. The institution firmed up plans to raise about one billion rupees before the end of the current fiscal through private placement of capital gains bonds and fixed deposits. Also, in order to keep the offer open for a longer duration, it planned to offer these bonds on tap through a public offer route.
NOVEL LUXURY TAX LEVIES LIKELY IN UNION BUDGET

The budget was likely to contain several innovative tax proposals that would mop up money in the form of expenditure tax. The taxes in the proposals included a $5,000 fee on non-resident Indians that would enable them to enjoy economic and business benefits. Also on the cards were taxes/levies on domestic air travel, telephone ownership, electricity consumption over a certain level, car ownership and property.
SURVEY SETS AGENDA TO KEEP ECONOMY ON COURSE

The Economic Survey of 1996/97 (April-March) called for an increase in crude oil prices and dismantling of the existing administered pricing mechanism in the sector. It also advocated removal of impediments to domestic and international trade in agriculture, raising resources from rich farmers to pay for public investment in rural infrastructure and restricting the primary deficit to zero level.
Business Standard
PANEL TO LOOK AT WAYS TO WIDEN TAX BASE

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda assured the ruling coalition that he would constitute an expert panel to suggest ways to increase the direct tax base and mobilise alternative resources. He said it was too late to change the forthcoming budget, but promised to look into the suggestions of the Left parties after it was presented to parliament on Friday.
HINDUSTAN PETROLEUM, INTEL PROPOSALS APPROVED

The Industry Ministry cleared 54 foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals amounting to about 7.85 billion rupees with export projections of over 29 billion rupees. These included a 1.75 billion rupee proposal by Volclay International for production of bentonite products and Hindustan Petroleum's 1.56 billion rupee proposal for a liquefied natural gas terminal and gas-fired power plant with Total. Intel Corp was allowed to invest 420 million rupees through a 100 percent subsidiary which would focus on development of software and a sales and marketing network for Intel products in India. RPG Telephone was allowed to bring in 102 million as FDI following a change in its shareholding patter
POPULATION GROWTH OUTPACES RISE IN FOODGRAIN OUTPUT

For the first time since the green revolution, foodgrains output growth lost the race against population increase. This was despite nine successive good monsoons and was attributed by the Economic Survey to the decline in public investment in the agriculture sector and the continuation of restrictive policies in farm goods trade. The annual compound growth rate of foodgrains output in the previous six years was estimated at 1.7 percent, short of the 1.9 percent population growth rate.
EASING OF MONEY SUPPLY RULED OUT

The Economic Survey warned against any further easing of money supply because the level of bank credit was not rising. With the development of the capital market and non banking financial system, savings in the form of bank deposits could no longer be equated with total financial savings, the survey said.
